utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The Chamber was informed that there are a few preliminary matters to be raised. Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Good morning. Before we begin with the next witness, I would like to make a request and I am seeking instruction. Yesterday we were in touch with our colleague, Mr. Weber, about using this witness's statements from the Karadzic case. We had a technical and a practical problem. In our submission under 92 ter, on the 12th of May 2014, we submitted a draft statement of this witness from the Karadzic case. And in the list of evidence that we planned to use with this witness, we submitted a modified version of this witness's statement from the Karadzic case which was modified in accordance with the additional statement taken by this witness. So yesterday we uploaded the signed version in B/C/S of this witness, and we talked with the witness about this, we informed the Prosecution about it, so we don't have any problem to have admitted into evidence this witness's statement submitted under 92 ter. But just for practical reasons, Your Honours, because of the overlap and better understanding of the witness, we submitted a statement by the witness from the Karadzic case. Both of these statements, I would say, are almost identical, but there is a difference in some paragraphs and in the text, just because it has been clarified in terms of using the statement from this witness from the Milosevic case. I don't know if I explained it in the best possible way, but this is my request, and I am seeking your instructions as to how we are going to be using this witness's statement from the Karadzic case for practical reasons, and we would like to tender it. As for us, we have our positions, and we are prepared to have both statements from the Karadzic case admitted as well as our additional statement from this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Well, initially just to keep matters simple and without going into too much detail, it's my understanding, and what we communicated to the Defence was we would not oppose the statement tendered with the 92 ter motion, provided that the witness attest to it, and that's what our position was in our response. So if that's what they are tendering, then that's okay. We did communicate that we would have objections based on the differences which the one we inadvertently discovered that was uploaded in e-court, which was different, albeit similar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, to be very practical, Mr. Weber. If we would -- if the original statement would be tendered, and if then we would hear viva voce all the -- what is now in the new version, what's the difference with admitting and tendering the newest version? You can still -- if it raises any questions, you can still compare the two and ask the witness or raise issues about what was changed. I mean, the one doesn't exclude the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: There is quite a -- just to go to probably what is the most significant difference, and it's one that relates to the transparency related to the witness's evidence which could impact on his credibility. In the one that was filed with the motion, the witness is quite clear that these are additions to matters that he discussed in the Milosevic testimony. So that is not part and not made clear as part of the statement that was then re-uploaded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: So there is many other that -- that then implicates other things within that statement. So we believe that the statement that was filed is more transparent and actually --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: -- would be better suited to allow the Chamber to assess the credibility of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, Mr. Weber, the Chamber doesn't want to receive all these statements into evidence. There are two options. Either you come with the first statement and then you have to elicit the evidence in addition to that, Mr. Stojanovic. There is another option, and we leave it in the hands of the Defence; that is, that you tender the last statement. And then, Mr. Weber, of course, you have a full opportunity to explore difference with the previous one, and you even could tender -- if it's significant, you could even tender the previous one, if that is necessary to understand the -- the changes, et cetera. At the same time, Mr. Stojanovic, the Chamber expresses its concerns. Concerns about what? Concerns about always new statements coming in. And especially that is of some concern because we've heard from one of the witnesses how it happens. Please, 10th of May, sign the statement, whatever changes, we'll deal with that at a later stage. That is not the appropriate way of giving notice to the -- to the Prosecution. That's what I just wanted to express as the concern of the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may just clarify. The two -- it's the -- the old and the new statement are from the Karadzic case. They were not modified by our team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then -- well, that may be -- statements taken for other cases may cause, here and there, some problems anyhow. But we'll just -- the Chamber would prefer to have the 92 ter statements produced at the time of the motion, the 92 ter motion, and rather rely on that to start with. And, of course, it's always possible that in proofing, there are some small differences but -- so we leave it in your hands, but only one statement to start with. And, Mr. Weber, if there is really any need, we'll certainly consider any tendering of portions of the previous statement. Or if you read it to the witness, or if you point at what was left out or what was added to the witness, that may certainly add to the transparency.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That's understood. I'd just note for the record, though, that might be a time-consuming process in a 30-paragraph statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If that turns out to be the case, then, of course, we'll take that into consideration when talking about time. Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Just one more thing. Yesterday when I asked the witness to sign the statement in accordance with my agreement with the Prosecutor, I asked him if he stood by what was said in the Milosevic transcript, so perhaps I can ask the witness the same question in order to clear this matter up when he begins his testimony. Perhaps we could do it like that. But in any event, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber will only admit signed statements; that's one. Second, it should be beyond any doubt what statement the witness attests to. And if there are differences, and if in a previous case he has attested to other versions, then, of course, that is a matter which certainly will need great attention. That was it for the next witness. Mr. Shin, we'll ask the witness to be escorted into the courtroom. I think you have 19 minutes left if I'm well informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Skrba.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Skrba, I'd like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony, and Mr. Shin will now continue his cross-examination. Mr. Shin, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Skrba.

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I'd like to continue this morning by returning to a document that we were looking at when we finished yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: That's 65 ter 30783.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And while we're waiting for that to come up, Mr. Skrba, you'll recall that this is the document signed by Major Savo Simic who is identified as a desk officer in the artillery organ.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now if we could turn briefly to the second page in the English and in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Under the heading "Ammunition Consumption," you see here that there are 40 shells listed for the 82-millimetre mortars and the same for the 120-millimetre. And for the support of the attack, there's 60 shells for each, totalling 100 shells for each, exactly as ordered by General Milosevic in that earlier document we saw yesterday. Have you seen those -- have you found those line items?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Skrba, when you were asked about this document in the Karadzic case, you were asked this question by the Prosecution: "Q. Do you accept --"

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Excuse me, that's transcript page 29215.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: "Q. Do you accept that there were areas within the area of operation of the 1st Smbr in the August of 1995 which might have contained 120-millimetre mortar positions that you were unaware of?" And you had stated: "I don't know anything about that. I wouldn't want to comment. I wouldn't want to answer that question because I don't know anything about it." You stand by your testimony in the Karadzic case; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now, would you also agree that you wouldn't have been aware of any operations elsewhere in the 1st Smbr's zone of responsibility which might have involved this 120-millimetre mortar battery?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Could you please repeat your question? A part of it is not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: My question to you is: This mortar battery, any other operations that it might have been conducting in the Smbr zone of responsibility, you wouldn't have any knowledge of that either, would you? Not in the positions that you held.

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. I was at my own position, and I don't know about any other actions that might have been under way.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Your Honours, with that, the Prosecution would tender 65 ter 30783.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30783 receives number P6602, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Skrba, I want to go back to something that you said yesterday. Now, you asserted several times yesterday that you did not know anything about mortars. You expressed little knowledge about mortars, about resupplying mortar units, despite the fact that you were in the last two years and couple months of the war assistant commander for logistics in your battalion command. You also made it clear that decisions about targeting and about which assets to use came from higher commands, not you as a company commander. You even said: "I really don't know much about mortars, and that's why I'm asking you to skip that topic." Yet, when you saw the Talas 2 order from General Milosevic - that was P6601 - you were quick to assert that the reference to a 120-millimetre mortar battery in Palez was a mistake. And you said it was a mistake because, actually, they were 82-millimetre mortars; because, actually, they were at the place you marked the 82-millimetre mortars you knew about and not in Palez; and because, actually, you say, the 120-millimetre mortars were actually at Prljevo Brdo, not Palez. On that basis, you concluded that that whole document was wrong. Mr. Skrba, I'm just going to put this to you directly. Now, while you may not always have been forthcoming in your knowledge about mortars, you actually have no basis of knowledge for asserting that General Milosevic and Major Simic were mistaken or that these documents share some type of typographical errors. You have no basis of knowledge for that assertion, do you?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I do have the knowledge. I mean, if I didn't see the mortars with my own eyes, it means that they were not there, and I still state with full responsibility that 120-millimetres were not there in the place where you mentioned where the village of Stamenkovici [phoen] is mentioned. Palez or Mala Kula was a small settlement. At the top of the hill of Palez, there were 82-millimetre mortars which I did see with my very own eyes, and that's why I said it. There were no 120-millimetre mortars there, and that is what I am asserting with 100 per cent certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And you explained that you passed by that place maybe once every two months. Maybe once or twice a month. You've explained that. So the times you weren't there, you wouldn't know what was there. That's obvious, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that 120-millimetre mortars are not an infantry weapon that you can carry it up and down and back and forth. Once it's placed, it's an artillery piece. From what I know, it has to be then kept in one place. It's not something that you would just carry around.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Skrba, once again, you say you know nothing about mortars but you're telling us about how mortars can be moved around. You have no basis of knowledge for that, do you?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was so. We didn't have a unit -- we didn't have them in the unit. We didn't use them. So I said I don't know much about mortars, but I know for a fact that they were not at that location in that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: The other thing you're doing, Mr. Skrba, is that you're putting in one location the 82-millimetre mortars that you saw and the 120-millimetre mortar battery that's a topic of these two documents, the order from General Milosevic and the implementing order from Major Simic. You have no basis of knowledge for claiming these are two -- these are one -- these two things are in one and the same place. You have no basis of knowledge for that, do you?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't that. I saw 82-millimetre mortars at a specific place at a specific position. 120-millimetre mortars were never at that place. I mean, the locals would have told me. Somebody would have told me had there been weapons there of that calibre because they lived there during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: The Judges now have the maps and they have the documents, so I'm going to move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I, nevertheless, ask one question. You emphasised again and again that you're certain that the place you indicated there were 82-millimetre mortars, that there were no 120-millimetre mortars there. Yesterday a part of your statement was put to you, and I read it again: "That is the only place on that road where there was mortar positions. I claim that at that, or other positions in the vicinity, there were no 120-millimetre mortars." Now, you explained to us yesterday that -- and you corrected even a written document, that at Prljevo Brdo there were 120-millimetre mortars. So now apart from the questions that were put to you by Mr. Shin, Prljevo Brdo is not far away from where you said the 82-millimetre mortars were, is it -- isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, that is not so. The reason why I didn't say it, I assume that -- I assume that there was a mistake between these two locations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Stop, one second --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were no mortars at my hill.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are not listening to my question very much. I asked you about the distance between Prljevo Brdo, where you said there were 120-millimetre mortars, and the place you indicated as the location where there were 82-millimetre mortars. My question was that it is not far away from the one place from the other, is it? And if you say it was far away, then tell us what the distance was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that it was about 5 kilometres as the crow flies. That was the distance. And along the road, it was 15 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now our maps tells that the -- and I think it was at Palez, isn't it, where the 82-millimetre mortars were, but I can check that. We'll just check on the map. Could you tell us again where -- and you -- I think you marked it, as a matter of fact, in D531. And I'm just -- Could we have a look at D531 on our screen, please. You marked the -- no, that's not the one on which I think you marked. Could we have a look at -- Could you perhaps -- we see Miljevici here on this map. You see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I'm a bit confused. One second, please. One second.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I marked the mortar positions at this cross-roads, leading to Studenkovici and to the top of Mount Trebevic, about 50 metres from the cross-roads along the macadam road. At the top of the hill called Palez, there is a small fort, and that's where these -- or small tower, and this is where these mortars were located. This is some 30 to 50 metres away from the cross-roads.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now you told us that Prljevo Brdo and this position at Palez, that it's a distance of 5 kilometres. Looking at our maps --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- it is -- yes, as the crow flies. I would say it's less than a kilometre. And we could have a look at -- let me just see. One second, please. Could we have a look at -- I have to reorganise myself. I think it is P56 -- no, P6599. Could we have a look at that map. Could we zoom in. Can you find Palez, which is just on the top line of the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This map doesn't show it properly. You're looking at the village of Studenkovici, from there to Prljevo Brdo. But Palez is at the very beginning of where the hill starts. This whole side is called Palez, below Studenkovici. I marked it next to the village of Studenkovici. This is where the 82-millimetre mortars were. I never said that they were on Palez.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Even then, let's take it from the place you marked. We see that now. Do you see Prljevo Brdo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you also see the grid lines which stand, if the parties would agree with that, for 1 kilometre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I think it's more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm seeking the agreement of the parties on what these grid lines stand for, whether it's 1 kilometre or more.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's -- it marks 1 kilometre as --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It marks 1 kilometre.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: -- Mr. President, you've correctly said. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, if you say it is 5 kilometres, I would suggest that it is anywhere between perhaps 11, 1200 metres as the crow flies. Any reason to challenge that? We could measure it in detail on the map, if you wish, but my main aim of our asking you this question is where you said 5 kilometres as the crow flies, that it's at least three times as much as it appears to be on this map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In my view and to my knowledge, that is the distance. I have never looked at these maps, but I know the location and I know the settlements. I think it is so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if you take the distance as the crow flies, maps are an excellent way of establishing what the distance is as the crow flies, and I do understand that you have a different opinion about that. Let's move on. Mr. Shin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you -- thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Skrba, I'd like to move to a different topic. Now, yesterday during the direct examination, you discussed humanitarian convoys. Now, first, in regard to humanitarian convoys, you said: "We did not even control them. There was a police check-point, a military police check-point, where they were checked."

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: That's at transcript 22788.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: It was, in fact, the military police who had such responsibilities and not your unit; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now, second, let's look at a map.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Could I please have P3, e-court page 76.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: While we're waiting for that, Mr. Skrba, I'm just explain what you're going to see is a map, which includes your zone of responsibility, the zone of responsibility when you were a company commander. Now, if you look at this map, you'll see -- almost in the centre, you see Debelo Brdo, you see a little bit to the right and further up Cicin Han. You see Lipe and Brekovac [phoen] in very small letters. Your positions were along this Lukavica-Pale road, which we see looping north of Palez and Zlatiste; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. From Zlatiste towards the north on Trebevic, so starting from Zlatiste.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: You see -- Mr. Skrba, you see where Palez is; right?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: We've already marked this on several maps. Would you simply agree with me that your zone of responsibility was along that stretch of road to north of Palez? We can see the Lukavica-Palez road there.

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrba. Now, you said the vehicles carrying humanitarian assistance passed through your company's zone of responsibility. You also explained that the convoys entered near the airport and in Grbavica. And we see on this map Grbavica to the north-west. You know this area very well. You see that; right?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: As we look at this map, there was no reason for a convoy going to Grbavica to go through your zone of responsibility, was there?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: You would agree with me that there is no reason for a humanitarian convoy going to Grbavica from the airport would pass through your zone of responsibility? Just so that we're clear.

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to explain. Those humanitarian convoys which went via Pale went through our territory, and they arrived in Lukavica. Those which were supposed to go to Grbavica and to the town itself were then diverted in that direction. Those going to the airport were diverted towards the airport. Not all convoys went to Grbavica and then returned to the airport. Those heading for Grbavica went there because they provided humanitarian assistance. Those that had to do -- go to the airport, did so. Not all convoys went to Grbavica and then further afield.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: That's clear, Mr. Skrba, but there were no convoys coming from -- just if you can listen to the question: There were to convoys, humanitarian convoys, going from the airport, to Grbavica, to the Brotherhood and Unity bridge, that passed through your zone of responsibility. That did not happen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I may intervene for a moment, there seems to be confusion. Mr. Skrba, when you're talking about the convoys, humanitarian aid convoys, you describe them as coming through Pale. From Pale going to Lukavica, and then from Lukavica back into town. That's how I understood your testimony. Now, did most of the humanitarian aid convoys, did they come through Pale, or did they arrive at the airport and were transported from there into the town of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know exactly where all -- they all went, but I know that those going through Pale were always cleared. They could go through without any problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You say they arrived over land at Pale?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then further went overland over the road you controlled - the Pale-Lukavica road - to Lukavica, and from there, they went into the town of Sarajevo. Is that how I have to understand your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because this Chamber has heard evidence of humanitarian aid convoys coming from different directions, not mainly through Pale. Could you give us any indication as to how frequent these humanitarian convoys came from Pale?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't say how frequently but they did pass through. Sometimes more frequently; at other times, less frequently. It depended on the UN schedule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you aware of other routes taken, either by plane or through other entries into the town of humanitarian aid convoys?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think there were air convoys as well as land convoys, but I don't know how many exactly. And I don't know which routes they all took.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And those air convoys didn't have to pass through your area of responsibility in order to reach the town of Sarajevo, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And there may have been other routes by land which did not pass through your area of responsibility in order to reach the city of Sarajevo; is that correct as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Shin, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: One more question on that topic, Mr. Skrba. Some of these other routes from Pale to the city of Sarajevo were more direct than this path that you've told us about going over land along the Lukavica-Pale road; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that was the only road.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Are you sure there was not a more direct route from Pale to Sarajevo? You know this area.

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only thing I know is that they went through the area I mentioned. I don't know about any others.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: We're going to go to a document now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Could I please have D462.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Skrba, while we're waiting for this document to come up, I'll tell you what it is. It's a document dated the 11th of April, 1994. It's from the Main Staff of the Army of the Republika Srpska to the president. And on the last page, we see that it is from Chief of Staff, General Milovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: If we could please turn to English page 5 and B/C/S page 3. Near the bottom of the page in B/C/S -- actually, it's probably -- I think it's in the middle of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Under the heading "Situation --" I'm sorry, in B/C/S, it is at the bottom of the page; middle of the page in English. Under the heading "Situation in Territory." I'll read to you what it says: "There were no movements of the teams and convoys of UNPROFOR and the humanitarian organisations across the RS territory during the day. The Main Staff of the VRS order a restriction of movement is being observed." Now, this is 1994. Were you -- at that time you were at the battalion command, were you aware of this Main Staff order?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never commanded a battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I did not say you commanded a battalion. I said you worked -- I said you worked at the command of a battalion. You've told us that. You were assistant logistics commander.

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I was never privy to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: So you knew nothing about that. A little further down, this is B/C/S page 4 --

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'll start again. Just to have a clear record here. If we could go to B/C/S page 4, English page 6. We're going to turn to the last paragraph here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And I'll read to you what it says. "Following the decision of the Supreme Command of the armed forces of the RS, all relations between the Main Staff of the Army of the Republika Srpska with the UN force command should be suspended. The restriction of movement for the teams and convoys of UNPROFOR and the humanitarian organisations is still in force." This restriction of movement, including all humanitarian organisations and UNPROFOR convoys, were you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: If I could just have one moment, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Just one final brief topic for you, Mr. Skrba. Now, you've said in your statement and in your testimony here that you were in the 2nd Battalion of the Smbr. Now that did cause some confusion, but this Chamber has heard evidence on the command structure of the 2nd Battalion. They've heard evidence that the commander was, first, Brane Pakalovic, and then Radomir Stojanovic, and then Aleksandar Petrovic. You've told us that Blagoje Kovacevic was your battalion commander and that Predrag Trapara was not in your battalion. So would you accept that, in fact, at least as of May 1993, you were in the 3rd Battalion, not the 2nd Battalion, as your statement says and as you've testified here several times?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a change. You are correct, though. At the end of the war, as of 1993, we were the 3rd Battalion, and then there was a change. They became the 1st Battalion, and they acted as the commanders of the 1st Battalion, and we became the 2nd Battalion. When you referred to that time, I was actually in the 3rd Battalion while they were in the 2nd. That was at the beginning of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I'll stop you there, Mr. Skrba. My question to you is this: Do you accept that as of May 1993 your battalion commander was Blagoje Kovacevic and you were, in fact, in the 3rd Battalion of the Smbr?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. In May 1993, it was Blagoje Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Shin. I would still like to revisit the matter of the distances and the markings by you, Mr. Skrba. Could I have on the screen, to the left-hand side, if possible; P6599, and on the right-hand side, D00526. Could it be enlarged slightly, especially to the left. Witness, I would like to invite you to look at the marking where you said the 82-millimetre mortars were on the left map; that is, just to the right of where the text reads Studenkovici. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you compare that with the marking on the map on the right where it says the 82-millimetre mortars were. Would you agree with me that your marking on the left map, if imposed on the map to the right, that your marking is between the letters E and V of the word Trebevic? Could someone -- has someone -- is it possible to [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you also agree with me that that's a distance of far more than 500 metres away from where you marked it in the previous case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I said is if you look at the right-hand side map, from the cross-roads with the macadam road, the mortars were some 50 to 70 metres away from it. On the left-hand side map, one doesn't see that. The left-hand side map, in my view, is not a good one. I don't know where it comes from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, first of all, the marking on the map to your left, which is P6599, the marking is made by yourself. And it's quite different from the marking you made in the previous case, which is found on D526. So if you say the other map is good as well, then that creates some confusion. It's at a considerable distance, the one from the other. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do. But this map is completely unclear to me, the left one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you marked it. You marked --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me tell you this, Percin. I know it. I know what it physically looks like. Where it says Percin, that hill is above Studenkovici. Studenkovici is at the foot, and it seems to be the other way around on this map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, they haven't moved north to south and changed it. I give you an opportunity to comment on the following. What is marked on D526, that is, the map, the right -- the map on your right-hand side, the marking there is corresponding almost entirely with the right upper corner of this figure where locations for, as I understand, artillery were marked before you marked that map. Would you agree with me, or would you have any comment on that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what these markings are. I have no clue. I can't even comment. As for what I marked, that is what I would dare comment. As for any other markings, I am clueless.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you made markings on both maps; one in the previous case, one in the present case. And I'm not asking you to explain the markings which were already on the map. I just put it to you that the marking on the right-hand side map, that is D526, is corresponding almost entirely to the pre-markings we find on P6599, that is the left-hand side, where there is an indication for a position. If you have no comments, we leave it to that. I further put to you that the distance from the marking on D526 to the position at Prljevo Brdo, if read together, the two maps, is approximately 800 metres, which could be understood as in the vicinity of the 82-millimetre mortars. Any comment on that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no comment. I know the area well. I hail from it and I know it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and I'm looking at the maps for distances. Judge Fluegge has a question for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: A short follow-up question. If you look on the right of this -- the map on the right side of the screen, you see there the square. Who has made this square? Did you do that with your own hands, or with a computer, or did that -- was that produced by somebody else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Someone else put that square in there. All I did was make markings in pen. I don't know about the rest, though.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I don't see any markings with a pen. Can you explain where the markings are to be seen you made with your own hands?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it may have been on another map. We would need to find it. It's not this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I put to you that in your statement, paragraph 15, you said in relation to this map on the right-hand side of the screen, I quote: "I marked with a square the area of the winding road and encircled the approximate place where there was an 82-millimetre mortar in August 1995." That is to be found in your statement which you'd signed. Did you make the marking, or was it a wrong statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a mistake. I made markings in pen. I hope you have that map, the other one, so that we can see my markings. I entered the location there. And this may be some kind of misinterpretation. I didn't make that particular marking. I don't have a computer to be able to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Was this map, as we see on the screen on the right-hand side, shown to you by the Defence team when you helped them to create this statement and before you signed the statement? Was this one shown to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And what was the -- does that correspond to another one you prepared with your own pen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: To be clear, we don't have this map you marked with your own hands.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think there should be one. I saw it yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The markings I made concerning the road going up Trebevic. We saw it yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Are you referring to a map where you can find this rectangle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I'm talking about some pen markings which I made on the map where the road diverts towards Trebevic and the location where the mortars were. So the map I marked is identical to the rectangle we see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In any case, what you said in your statement, which you signed, it's in relation to this document, and I read that to you: "In this document, I marked with a square the area of the winding road," which was not done by yourself. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Shin, you were on your feet but you are sitting down now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yeah, sorry. I just was wondering if this might be helpful. The witness may be confused, or I may be confused, but on the left-hand map here, the -- there is handwriting in the middle. Of course --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's his marking he made in court.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes, if that's clear to Your Honours, then I'll --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's perfectly clear. I think I hinted at the considerable distance between what he marked yesterday --

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and what we see on the map that was related to his statement about the square and the MB 82 millimetre, which is at quite a different location.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes. And I fully appreciate the thrust of Your Honour's questions. I just wanted to clarify also that on a minor issue that I do believe that he had marked this previously, as we see in the date in the lower right-hand corner, the 22nd of October, and I believe the rest of that will show it's 2012.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Stojanovic, any further questions for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a few questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it is a matter of minutes, then I would allow you to proceed. If you say it's more than two or three minutes, we would take a break first.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, I suggest we go on a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then I would like to ask the usher to escort the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And to avoid any confusion, the date you referred to, Mr. Shin, was on the original map from which a portion was taken into D526, and that original map bears number P6597.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: If I could just have a moment to check that, but if I understood Your Honour's question correctly, the -- it's, of course, and perhaps I've my misunderstood, but it's the witness who has written 22/10/2012.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, apparently he marked already at that time --

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- a map which shows a similar rectangle with a similar MB 82-millimetre mortar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I see. I understand the issue, then, and I will see if there is anything of further assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We take a break, and we will resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Shin, the preliminary matter -- one second, please, Mr. Usher. One second. The preliminary matter you wanted to raise, should that be in the presence of the witness or in his absence?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: We can do it in the absence, and Your Honours can -- we can figure out how to -- whether we need to address it when the witness arrives as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: It's quite brief. I just wanted to clarify, on further discussion with my colleagues, the map where we had discussed that one grid was 1 kilometres, it may be 2. It appears, in fact, to be 2. We will confirm that. But, of course, that still makes a significant difference between 5 kilometres or one grid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: But I wanted to make that clarification as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If it is 2 then --

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm only very happy that you -- you would correct that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes. I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think I oriented myself on the other map with the blue lines, which I always thought was 1 kilometre; but if I'm wrong, then I sincerely apologise to both parties for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And our apologies for not catching that earlier, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. That --

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's fine. Well, could I say the following - Mr. Stojanovic, I'm also addressing you - the witness apparently assesses distances from his knowledge of the local situation. Although he says "as the crow flies," do we agree that to measure distances as the crow flies is better done on maps than by a vague recollection of the terrain?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: We would certainly agree with that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will concur that a map is better than memory or just an assessment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which doesn't say anything about what it takes to travel from one point to another, which may be considerably more, especially in mountainous terrain. Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Meanwhile, the Chamber invited the Defence yesterday to express itself on the revised translation of P3059.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We checked, Your Honour, and we can accept that translation as relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And better than the previous one, I take it. Madam Registrar, the translation attached to P3059 should be replaced by doc ID 0528-8804-00ET, and you're hereby instructed to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic. Mr. Skrba, you'll -- further questions will be put to you by Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we please have document P6597 in e-court. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Skrba, this area that has these serpentines, these curves, is that the road that you marked to Trebevic?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And the village of Studenkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: This red line on the left that is an arrow moving towards the centre of Studenkovic, does it actually denote the road that you marked as leading to Studenkovic?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it says here Studenkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: This little circle and this arrow underneath MB 82 mm, meaning millimetres, does that show the approximately accurate location where you saw the 82-millimetre mortars?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Shin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, we're having several very leading questions now. I was not going to stand up for the first couple, but if we could please stay away from those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, you're invited not to lead the witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I will try to organise this in a different way, just that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Skrba, when speaking to me when I showed you this map, did you confirm that this little circle corresponds to the position of the mortar?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's another leading question, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. I'll reorganise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: During proofing, Mr. Skrba, did you inform the Defence about whether this map and these markings were drawn to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we now please take a look at this together as we saw it before. P6599, along parallel lines, with D516. D526. Your Honours, P6599, could we slightly enlarge the central part. Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Skrba, appreciating the work that you have been doing so far, are you knowledgeable about geographical maps?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In August 1995, did you have at any point in time any personal knowledge to the effect that there were mortars of 82 millimetres in the broader area of Studenkovic?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did have such knowledge and that's why I marked this place where they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it possible, if we look at the left-hand map there, this point that is to the north-east of 1231, if you can see that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Were there 82-millimetre mortars there in the summer of 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were there until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: These mortars -- actually, does this change your view regarding the existence of 82-millimetre mortars on the location that you marked on this map on the right-hand side, that is, 50 to 70 metres away from the road to Studenkovici and the intersection?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't change anything. It is the same position that I marked on both maps as far as I can see and as far as I can read these maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to conclude with the following question: After having marked these two positions of 82-millimetre mortars, does that change anything in terms of your answer that in the area of the village of Studenkovici, there was no 120-millimetre mortars?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't change anything, and I've been saying all along that in the area of the village of Studenkovic there were never any 120-millimetre mortars.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, now I would just like us to take a look at yet another document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Before these maps are replaced by other documents, I would just clarify the last couple of answers of the witness. Are you saying that on both maps we see on the screen the locations are at the same spot, the locations indicated by you on the two maps.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I really don't understand this because obviously what we see is Studenkovici on the right-hand side of the screen quite far away and more to the south than on the left-hand side of the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the left-hand side, there is no road. I mean, the little road. I mean, the intersection is there nearby. You see this. 12331, that's the village. That's that feature. So then that is where you turn off to the village, at that curve, and that is why I marked the curve there on the left-hand side. And then from the curve, 50 to 70 metres away there are these mortars. I mean, the ones that I marked on this right-hand side. In my view, it's one and the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I hear that, but obviously when I look on these two maps the locations are quite different. The little circle is far away from Studenkovici on the right-hand side of the screen and that differs quite a lot from the left marking you personally made.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This map on the right-hand side is enlarged and the other one is not, you see? You see this curve here, where you can see it here. It's the same curve on the left and on the right. And from there, you turn to Studenkovici. And there, at that curve, that's where the mortars were. I think that that's the place, in my view.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Identical place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may, lest there be any confusion, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: This is my question: In August 1995, to the best of your recollection and in terms of what you think - forget about the maps now - were there 82-millimetre mortars at two locations? From the intersection where the road goes to Studenkovic, and Studenkovic itself?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there was just one.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That's what I wanted to ask you. The next thing I wanted to ask --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we please have in e-court a document that is now marked as D -- I think it's 5 now, 5-9 ... just a second. 528.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's a D number?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D528. That's the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, can you recognise this photograph and what is seen in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us what the name of this feature is?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is part of Baba Stijene. It's just part of it. It's not the elevation itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And this will be my final question. At any point from 1992 to 1995, did you ever have any of your troops positioned there?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Did we have troops there? Yes, yes, there were troops there on both sides of Baba Stijene.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And on the feature of Baba Stijene itself?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your previous answer. "Did we have troops there? Yes, yes, there were troops there on both sides of Baba Stijene." Was that where the -- part of the answer was missed? I'm addressing the interpreters. Or was it the next question?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: It was the whole answer following the last question by Mr. Stojanovic, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So then Mr. Stojanovic asked you: "And on the feature of Baba Stijene itself?" Could you repeat your answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We did not have any trenches or any activities at Baba Stijene itself. It's a very steep rock, and it was not suitable for any kind of action.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And I will finish with the following question: Did you notice if any other unit, or a member of any other unit of the Army of Republika Srpska, at any point fired from the Baba Stijene position, either from a sniper rifle or any other type of infantry weapon?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. With your leave, Your Honour, I'd like to read out a short summary of this witness's statement. Witness Stevan Veljovic was assistant Chief of Staff for operations and training in the 1st Romanija Brigade between the beginning of the war and December 1994. He then joined the SRK staff staying in the same capacity. He remained there until 7 August 1995 when he assumed the duty of commander of the 4th Sarajevo Light Infantry Brigade. The witness claims that throughout the war, while acting as officer in the brigade and corps staffs, he never received or issued an order to shell civilian facilities or civilians in the area of Sarajevo but to shell military targets solely and exclusively. Legitimate military targets were established by direct observation or through intelligence work, although the units of the BH Army made use of different civilian facilities as points of resistance, especially the Kosevo hospital and the part of town called Bascarsija. They usually did so by using a truck mounted with a mortar and opened fire before moving on to another position. The points from which they used artillery were Zagrebacka Street, Marsala Tita Street, the road above the Marsal Tito Barracks, and areas close to UNPROFOR facilities to name but a few. All officers and soldiers of the brigade were made familiar with numerous written and oral orders issued by the senior command about the prohibition of opening fire on civilians, civilian facilities, and means of public transport. Every commander had a booklet about the international laws of war in the form of a brochure. There could have been civilian casualties only if strong artillery fire was opened from specific areas which placed VRS units in danger. In conclusion, the witness will testify that at the time of the so-called Markale II incident on 28th August, 1995, there was not a single 120-millimetre mortar piece in the area of defence of his brigade in the sector of Trebevic on Vidikovac and below the bobsleigh track on Trebevic. Such assets had been sent to assist the Herzegovina Corps of the VRS on 24 August 1995 where they stayed until September 1995. The witness directly participated in receiving orders from General Mladic personally to enable an unhindered and efficient passage through VRS-controlled territory to the convoy with the Zepa and Gorazde wounded in April 1995. Thank you. This was the short summary of this witness's statement. With your leave, I have a few questions to put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
